Study_Title: MPMA: Preference Manipulation Attack Against Model Context Protocol
Threat_Attacker_Model: Third-party MCP server publisher who manipulates tool names and metadata descriptions using direct persuasive phrases or genetic-algorithm-optimized subliminal advertising strategies (MPMA) to hijack LLM tool-selection preferences without user awareness (Figures 1–2, pp. 2–3).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Manipulative Preference Manipulation Attack / MPMA using Genetic Algorithm multi-objective stealthiness and persuasiveness optimization on MCP server descriptions; Figures 1–2, pp. 2–3).
Enforcement_Point_Location: MCP Tool Discovery & LLM Tool-Selection Ranking Layer (Figure 1, p. 2)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Violates fair tool-selection integrity and steers LLM agents toward attacker-controlled third-party MCP servers with up to 100% Attack Success Rate (ASR) while maintaining stealthiness (pp. 1–6).
Trust_Assumptions: Victim LLM agent discovers multiple candidate MCP servers providing overlapping functionality (e.g., on Smithery / open MCP registries) and ranks them via natural-language tool descriptions.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across multiple LLMs and MCP tool registries (AAAI 2026): direct persuasive insertion achieves near-100% ASR in most settings, while Genetic Algorithm (GA)-based subliminal advertising achieves both high ASR and high stealthiness against detection filters (Abstract & Section 1, pp. 1–2; Section 4, pp. 5–8).
Exposed_Security_Function: Preference Manipulation Attack (MPMA) benchmark and Genetic Algorithm stealthy description optimization against MCP tool selection
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Targets competitive multi-server tool selection when functionally equivalent MCP tools coexist in the prompt context; does not bypass deterministic user-pinned server allowlists.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Section 1 (pp. 1–3, Figures 1–2) and Section 4 (pp. 5–8): "MPMA: Preference Manipulation Attack Against Model Context Protocol... proves highly effective, achieving a 100% Attack Success Rate (ASR) in most settings... we utilize a Genetic Algorithm (GA) to optimize advertising strategies to achieve good stealthiness while ensuring a high ASR."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: MPMA manipulates MCP tool names and descriptions via direct insertion and Genetic Algorithm-optimized subliminal advertising, achieving up to 100% ASR in biasing LLM tool selection toward attacker-controlled MCP servers.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical evaluation of MCP tool-selection preference manipulation in AAAI 2026 (9 pp.)
Protected_Object: MCP tool discovery rankings, tool metadata descriptions, and LLM server selection decisions
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates how subtle persuasive phrasing injected at MCP server registration/discovery (B2) biases downstream tool invocation routing without altering user prompts (Figures 1–2, pp. 2–3).
Coding_Rationale: Makalah AAAI 2026 (9 hlm.) yang memperkenalkan Preference Manipulation Attack (MPMA) pada deskripsi alat MCP dengan ASR hingga 100% dan optimisasi kesenyapan berbasis Algoritma Genetika.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: MSA: A Cross-MCP Privacy Attack via Memory Exfiltration of Large Language Models
Threat_Attacker_Model: Cross-MCP malicious tool server (MSA) that embeds parasitic parameter schemas (e.g., task_history: str in @mcp.tool() functions such as debug_code_snippet or validate_api_response, p. 6) to siphon conversational memory and outputs from co-installed benign MCP servers (Figures 1–2, pp. 2–3).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Memory Siphoning Attack / MSA exploiting shared LLM context windows and over-scoped MCP tool parameter schemas across multiple MCP servers; Figures 1–2, pp. 2–3; p. 6).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Cross-MCP Shared LLM Context Window & Tool Argument Serialization Layer (Figures 1–2, pp. 2–3)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Violates cross-MCP server isolation and user conversation confidentiality by exfiltrating interaction histories through legitimate-looking tool parameters (pp. 1–6).
Trust_Assumptions: Victim LLM agent connects concurrently to benign MCP servers and at least one attacker-controlled MCP server within a shared session memory context.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across multiple LLMs and MCP server combinations (ACM WPES '25, pp. 1–6): MSA achieves a 100% Context Capture Rate (CCR) and 100% Exfiltration Success Rate (ESR), with cross-MCP memory reconstruction accuracy/fidelity ranging from 85.67% to 87.81% (Abstract & Section 1, pp. 1–2).
Exposed_Security_Function: Cross-MCP Memory Siphoning Attack (MSA) via parasitic tool parameter schemas (`task_history`)
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Requires the malicious MCP tool to be invoked at least once during the session and relies on the absence of per-server context compartmentalization or argument taint tracking.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Section 1 (pp. 1–3, Figures 1–2) and Appendix (p. 6): "MSA achieves a 100% context capture and exfiltration success rate, with memory reconstruction accuracy ranging from 85.67% to 87.81%... Examples of Tool Functions from Malicious MCP Servers: @mcp.tool() def debug_code_snippet(code_block: str, task_history: str) -> str."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: The Cross-MCP Memory Siphoning Attack (MSA) uses parasitic tool arguments (such as task_history) to achieve 100% context capture and exfiltration success with 85.67%–87.81% memory reconstruction accuracy.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical cross-MCP memory exfiltration attack evaluation in ACM WPES '25 (6 pp.)
Protected_Object: Cross-server LLM session memory, user conversation history, and benign MCP server outputs
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates cross-server composition where outputs from benign MCP servers stored in shared agent memory (B4) are serialized into parasitic tool parameters (`task_history`) of a malicious MCP server at discovery/invocation (B2/B3) (Figures 1–2, pp. 2–3; p. 6).
Coding_Rationale: Makalah ACM WPES '25 (6 hlm.) yang mendemonstrasikan serangan lintas-server MCP (MSA) dengan 100% CCR/ESR dan akurasi rekonstruksi memori 85,67%–87,81% melalui argumen fungsi parasit.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Multi-Context Protocol (MCP) Hosts provide secure and real-time integration of AI tools
Threat_Attacker_Model: Unauthorized external tool/API invocations, unencrypted transport eavesdropping, and unapproved execution of sensitive tools by AI agents (pp. 1–3).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Permission-gated MCP Host and API Gateway architecture enforcing TLS 1.2 transport encryption, OAuth 2.0 bearer authentication, MCP Inspector schema validation, and explicit user/policy permission gating prior to external REST API execution (Figures 1–4, pp. 2–3).
Enforcement_Point_Location: MCP Host, MCP Inspector, and Enterprise API Gateway (Figures 1–4, pp. 2–3)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: 100% rejection of unauthorized tool requests, authenticated TLS 1.2 / OAuth 2.0 transport, and auditable permission-gated execution (p. 4).
Trust_Assumptions: API Gateway, OAuth 2.0 authorization server, and MCP Host permission prompts are trusted.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Reports 2.1 s average end-to-end tool execution latency, 100% unauthorized request rejection rate, and 95% accurate LLM tool selection mapping across evaluated REST API workflows (Section IV-F, p. 4).
Exposed_Security_Function: TLS 1.2 + OAuth 2.0 API Gateway mediation, MCP Inspector validation, and permission-gated MCP Host execution
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on TLS 1.2 / OAuth 2.0 and manual/basic permission prompts; explicitly notes in Section V (p. 6) that conditional policy-based auto-approval and behavioral anomaly detection remain future work.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Figures 1–4 (pp. 2–3), and Section IV (p. 4): "The architecture integrates MCP Clients, Servers, and Hosts, coordinated via an API Gateway enforcing TLS 1.2, OAuth 2.0, and enterprise authentication... Real-time execution: 2.1 s avg. latency; Security enforcement: 100% unauthorized rejections; LLM tool selection: 95% correct mapping."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: An MCP Host architecture integrated with an OAuth 2.0 and TLS 1.2 API Gateway and MCP Inspector achieves 100% unauthorized request rejection, 95% tool selection accuracy, and 2.1 s average end-to-end execution latency.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Prototype MCP Host + API Gateway evaluation on real-time REST API tool workflows in IEEE ICCA 2025 (6 pp.)
Protected_Object: MCP tool invocations, OAuth 2.0 credentials, and external REST API endpoints
Composition_Evidence: Chains explicit user permission approval at the MCP Host (B1) with MCP Inspector schema validation and TLS 1.2 + OAuth 2.0 API Gateway enforcement (B3) and audit logging (B4) (Figures 1–4, pp. 2–3).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream A (IEEE ICCA 2025, 6 hlm.) yang melaporkan metrik terukur (2,1 dtk rata-rata latensi E2E, 100% penolakan akses tidak sah, 95% akurasi pemetaan alat) pada arsitektur MCP Host + OAuth 2.0/TLS 1.2 API Gateway.

Study_Title: Multi-Layer Collaborative Continuous Defense in PDNs Driven by an LLMInteractive Endpoint Trusted Intelligence Agent

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Multi-Layer Collaborative Continuous Defense (MCCD) driven by an LLM-Interactive Endpoint Trusted Intelligence Agent, combining Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) hierarchical attestation/execution (p. 9) and Temporal-Contextual Hierarchical Encoding (TCHE) transforming raw event streams into structured Semantic Security Intelligence (SSI) (Figures 1–2, pp. 6–8).
Enforcement_Point_Location: TEE-Protected Endpoint Trusted Intelligence Agent & End-Cloud Collaborative PDN Defense Layer (Figures 1–2, pp. 6–7)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Tamper-resistant endpoint telemetry encoding inside TEE, reduced semantic entropy of transmitted intelligence, and high multi-stage intrusion detection accuracy (AUC 0.963, F1 0.946; p. 15).
Trust_Assumptions: Endpoint hardware TEE roots of trust are intact and end-cloud collaborative channels authenticate TEE-signed SSI summaries.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Streamlined hierarchical TEE pipeline minimizes enclave memory/compute overhead and damage latency (p. 9), while achieving 0.963 AUC and 0.946 F1-score on DARPA-style host/PDN intrusion benchmarks (Section 4, p. 15).
Exposed_Security_Function: TEE-backed Endpoint Trusted Intelligence Agent and Temporal-Contextual Hierarchical Encoding (TCHE) for continuous PDN defense
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated on DARPA-style host and simulated power distribution network traces rather than live substation SCADA hardware under zero-day TEE side-channel attacks.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Section 2–3 (pp. 6–9, Figures 1–2) & Section 4 (p. 15): "Fig. 1. MCCD System Architecture... Fig. 2 illustrates the TCHE pipeline from raw event streams to structured SSI... to avoid unnecessary overhead within the TEE, we design a streamlined hierarchical pipeline... achieving overall performance of AUC 0.963 and F1 0.946."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: The MCCD framework with a TEE-protected LLM-Interactive Endpoint Trusted Intelligence Agent and TCHE encoding achieves 0.963 AUC and 0.946 F1-score in continuous power distribution network defense while minimizing TEE overhead.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: End-cloud collaborative TEE + LLM agent defense evaluated on PDN and DARPA-style intrusion benchmarks in KSII TIIS (2026, 22 pp.)
Protected_Object: PDN endpoint telemetry streams, TEE-encoded Semantic Security Intelligence (SSI), and grid control actions
Composition_Evidence: Couples TEE-isolated endpoint event encoding (TCHE at B3/B4) with end-cloud LLM-interactive collaborative threat reasoning and continuous defense orchestration (B2) (Figures 1–2, pp. 6–7).
Coding_Rationale: Artikel jurnal KSII TIIS (Mei 2026, 22 hlm.) yang memadukan agen intelijen endpoint berbasis TEE dengan pengodean TCHE dan melaporkan AUC 0,963 serta F1 0,946 pada evaluasi deteksi intrusi.

Study_Title: Operator-Blind Secret Mediation for AI Agents: A Formal Model and FHE Construction for Credential Derivation on Untrusted Infrastructure
Threat_Attacker_Model: Prompt injection, skill/MCP poisoning, tool misuse, and an honest-but-curious or untrusted hosted broker operator attempting to extract tenant master secrets (API keys, SSH credentials), with the small trusted tenant gateway excluded from root/kernel compromise (pp. 1–2, 8–9).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: CapSeal split-broker architecture combining a trusted tenant gateway, session-bound non-exportable capability handles, typed HTTP/SSH executors with schema validation, replay protection, revocation epochs, and tamper-evident audit logging, plus FHE-encrypted master secret storage (`TFHE-rs`) and LowMC/Rasta transciphering designs (pp. 1, 8–18).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Trusted Tenant Gateway, Operator FHE Deriver, and Typed HTTP/SSH Executors (pp. 8–18)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Theorem 1 proves computational operator blindness (confidentiality of the tenant master secret against the operator) under IND-CPA security of the FHE scheme; Theorem 2 proves conditional capability binding assuming a secure PRF/MAC instantiation (pp. 16–18).
Trust_Assumptions: Tenant gateway OS/process isolation, FHE decryption key custody, and policy/execution path are trusted; FHE scheme is IND-CPA secure; capability binding requires a cryptographically secure PRF/MAC (pp. 8–9, 16–18).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: In the operator-trusted broker path (Table 12, p. 29, n=500), median broker mediation overhead is 0.149 ms for HTTP and 0.208 ms for SSH; in the operator-blind FHE path (n=7), median latency is 8,970 ms for HTTP and 8,638 ms for SSH (~9 s per request).
Exposed_Security_Function: Session-bound non-exportable capability handles, FHE master-secret encryption (IND-CPA Theorem 1), and conditional PRF/MAC capability derivation (Theorem 2)
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Theorem 2 capability binding is conditional on instantiating a cryptographically secure PRF/MAC (whereas the prototype benchmark uses a 16-round mult-XOR non-cryptographic stand-in, pp. 1, 18, 33); active operator deviations can cause availability/integrity failures; FHE alone does not constitute end-to-end PQC migration.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Sections 3–5 (pp. 8–18, Theorems 1–2), and Section 8 (p. 29, Table 12; p. 33): "We formalize the model and prove computational operator blindness from IND-CPA security of the FHE scheme (Theorem 1), together with conditional capability binding for any secure PRF/MAC instantiation (Theorem 2)... Table 12: operator-trusted overhead median HTTP 0.149 ms, SSH 0.208 ms (n=500)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: CapSeal replaces direct agent credential access with non-exportable capability handles and proves computational operator blindness under IND-CPA FHE (Theorem 1) and conditional capability binding under secure PRF/MACs (Theorem 2), with 0.149 ms HTTP and 0.208 ms SSH median overhead on the operator-trusted path.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal split-broker security reductions (Theorems 1–2) and operator-trusted HTTP/SSH mediation benchmark (n=500) in MDPI Mathematics 2026, 14, 2434
Protected_Object: Tenant master secret ciphertexts, derived API/SSH credentials, and capability-bound request artifacts
Composition_Evidence: Composes session-bound capability handle issuance and operator-blind FHE derivation (B2) with typed HTTP/SSH executor mediation, replay/epoch checks (B3), and tamper-evident audit logging (B4) (pp. 1, 8–18).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-A) dari baris pilot EXTRACTED (CLM-0001 / SLR-M-0219): memisahkan model formal dan bukti reduksi Theorem 1 (IND-CPA operator blindness) & Theorem 2 (conditional PRF/MAC capability binding) beserta jalur broker operator-trusted (0,149 ms HTTP / 0,208 ms SSH) dari klaim benchmark prototipe stand-in FHE (-B), sambil menyelaraskan Formal_Evidence_Type ke THEORETIC_PROOF.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Operator-Blind Secret Mediation for AI Agents: A Formal Model and FHE Construction for Credential Derivation on Untrusted Infrastructure
Threat_Attacker_Model: Performance, latency, and cryptographic instantiation trade-offs when crossing the operator-untrusted FHE derivation boundary vs. TEE and MPC alternatives (Abstract, p. 1; Table 12, p. 29; p. 33).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: End-to-end TFHE-rs split-broker prototype evaluating operator-blind derivation using a 16-round mult-XOR non-cryptographic homomorphic stand-in alongside LowMC/Rasta transciphering analysis (pp. 1, 18, 29, 33).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Operator TFHE-rs Homomorphic Evaluation Service & Tenant Gateway Decryption Boundary (pp. 18–29)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Quantifies the exact computational cost of operator-blind FHE secret mediation (~9 s per request, ~17 million times slower than plaintext) and explicitly documents the gap between the non-cryptographic stand-in circuit and a full cryptographic PRF/MAC (pp. 1, 29, 33).
Trust_Assumptions: Prototype benchmark uses a 16-round mult-XOR non-cryptographic stand-in to measure TFHE-rs circuit traversal cost (Abstract, p. 1; p. 33).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Table 12 (p. 29): operator-blind TFHE-rs path incurs a median latency of 8,970 ms for HTTP and 8,638 ms for SSH (n=7, ~9 s per request, roughly 17 million times slower than the 0.149 ms / 0.208 ms plaintext/operator-trusted path).
Exposed_Security_Function: TFHE-rs homomorphic credential-derivation benchmark and FHE vs. TEE/MPC assurance-latency comparison
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: The benchmarked operator-blind TFHE-rs path uses a 16-round mult-XOR non-cryptographic stand-in rather than a validated cryptographic PRF/MAC (creating an internal tension between p. 1/p. 33 and p. 18's statement that 256-bit pseudorandomness/collision-resistance premises hold), and ~9 s per-request latency is prohibitive for high-frequency interactive tool calls.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Section 5 (p. 18), Section 8 (p. 29, Table 12), and Section 9 (p. 33): "The prototype uses a non-cryptographic homomorphic stand-in and measures the cost of crossing the operator-untrusted boundary at about 9 s per request, roughly 17 million times slower than the plaintext path... Table 12: operator-blind latency median HTTP 8970 ms, SSH 8638 ms (n=7)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: The TFHE-rs operator-blind CapSeal prototype incurs median request latencies of 8,970 ms (HTTP) and 8,638 ms (SSH) (n=7, ~17M times slower than plaintext) using a 16-round mult-XOR homomorphic stand-in.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical TFHE-rs prototype benchmark (n=7) and stand-in circuit limitation analysis in MDPI Mathematics 2026
Protected_Object: FHE-encrypted master secrets and homomorphically derived per-request tokens
Composition_Evidence: Quantifies the latency penalty of composing untrusted operator FHE evaluation (B2) with tenant-gateway decryption and typed HTTP/SSH execution (B3) (Table 12, p. 29).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-B) untuk SLR-M-0219: memisahkan temuan benchmark empiris jalur operator-blind TFHE-rs (8.970 ms HTTP / 8.638 ms SSH, n=7) dan konflik internal penggunaan non-cryptographic stand-in (hlm. 1 & 33 vs. hlm. 18) sebagai PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED (DG;AD;UG) pada RQ3.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Parasites in the Toolchain: A Large-Scale Analysis of Attacks on the MCP Ecosystem
Threat_Attacker_Model: Malicious or vulnerable third-party MCP servers conducting MCP Unauthorized Privacy Disclosure (MCP-UPD), tool poisoning, command injection, and cross-tool privilege escalation across public MCP ecosystems (Figures 1–2, pp. 3–4).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Large-scale static capability/taint analysis and dynamic LLM verification pipeline auditing 1,360 MCP servers and 12,230 tools from Pulse MCP, MCP Market, and Awesome MCP Servers; Section 4, pp. 6–8).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Ecosystem-Wide Static & Dynamic MCP Toolchain Security Auditor (pp. 6–14)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Identifies and dynamically verifies parasitic/vulnerable tools across 12,230 real-world MCP tools and evaluates multi-LLM susceptibility (GPT-4o, GPT-5, Claude-4.5-Sonnet, DeepSeek-R1, Gemini-2.5-Flash; pp. 2, 8, 18).
Trust_Assumptions: Public MCP registries (Pulse MCP 57.6%, MCP Market 22.8%, Awesome MCP Servers 19.6%, p. 8) host unvetted third-party server code and tool definitions.

Exposed_Security_Function: Large-scale three-capability static/dynamic security audit of 1,360 MCP servers and 12,230 tools
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Focuses on offensive/diagnostic ecosystem measurement and vulnerability discovery across 12,230 tools rather than deploying a cryptographic runtime enforcement gateway.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Section 1 (pp. 1–3, Figures 1–2), Section 4 (pp. 6–8), and Section 5 (p. 18): "we systematically analyze 1,360 MCP servers and 12,230 tools from Pulse MCP (784 servers, 6,736 tools), MCP Market (310 servers, 2,781 tools), and Awesome MCP Servers (266 servers, 2,713 tools), identifying 1,062 risky tools (8.7% of 12,230) across 370 servers (27.2%)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: A large-scale audit of 1,360 real-world MCP servers and 12,230 tools reveals that 27.2% of servers (370) and 8.7% of tools (1,062) harbor exploitable privacy-disclosure and toolchain vulnerabilities.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Large-scale empirical vulnerability measurement across 1,360 MCP servers (12,230 tools) and 6 frontier LLMs (SJTU, HKUST, Chaitin Tech, 18 pp.)

Coding_Rationale: Studi skala besar (18 hlm.) yang mengaudit 1.360 server MCP dan 12.230 alat dari 3 registri publik serta menemukan 370 server (27,2%) dan 1.062 alat (8,7%) bermasalah.

Study_Title: PlanTwin: Privacy-Preserving Planning Abstractions for Cloud-Assisted LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Honest-but-curious or untrusted cloud LLM planners observing sensitive local environment state (private source code, filenames, credentials, topological metadata) during multi-turn cloud-assisted agent planning (Figure 1, p. 3).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: PlanTwin privacy-preserving planning abstraction layer that maintains a sanitized structural twin for the cloud planner while keeping concrete state local (mediated by a local Qwen3.5-family model), proving (k, delta)-anonymity (Theorem 1) and epsilon-unlinkability (Theorem 2) with sequential composition across T turns (Eq. 37, pp. 14, 18).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Local PlanTwin Abstraction & Concretization Gateway between Local Environment and Cloud LLM Planner (Figure 1, p. 3)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: (k, delta)-anonymity (Theorem 1), epsilon-unlinkability (Theorem 2), and synthetic-population privacy bounds (Proposition 6.1, p. 14) across multi-turn cloud planning.
Trust_Assumptions: Local PlanTwin gateway and local small model (Qwen3.5-family) execute inside the user's trusted local boundary.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Achieves privacy protection scores > 0.79 while the full PlanTwin pipeline incurs less than 2.2% task utility loss compared to unredacted cloud planning (Abstract, p. 1; Section 5.4, Table 6, p. 8).
Exposed_Security_Function: Privacy-preserving structural planning abstraction with provable (k, delta)-anonymity (Theorem 1) and epsilon-unlinkability (Theorem 2)
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Equivalence-class size |EC_t| decays exponentially over T turns as fields in F_t are revealed (`|EC_t| >= |EC_{t-1}| e^{-Delta_t(o)}`, Eq. 37, p. 18), requiring periodic re-abstraction on very long-horizon tasks.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Figure 1 (p. 3), Section 6 (p. 14, Proposition 6.1, Theorems 1–2), and Appendix (p. 18, Eq. 37): "Proposition 6.1 (Synthetic-population privacy bound): (1) The (k, delta)-anonymity bound (Theorem 1) holds... (2) The epsilon-unlinkability bound (Theorem 2) holds... privacy score > 0.79, and the full pipeline incurs less than 2.2% utility loss."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: PlanTwin decouples cloud LLM planning from private local execution states via structural planning abstractions, proving (k, delta)-anonymity (Theorem 1) and epsilon-unlinkability (Theorem 2) with < 2.2% utility loss.

Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: High-risk tier escalations require human-in-the-loop approval latency, and classical ECDSA/Ed25519 JWT-SVID/DPoP signatures remain pre-quantum.

Study_Title: Runtime Policy Enforcement for MCP-Based LLM Agents

Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Exhibits a 30.0% task-level false-positive rate on complex benign workflows (Abstract, p. 1) and struggles to distinguish malicious tail truncation of an audit log from a legitimately short or aborted session without an external checkpoint anchor (p. 22).

Study_Title: SC-A2A Gateway: A Blockchain-Powered Gateway for Session Grants and Audit in Agent-to-Agent Collaboration
Threat_Attacker_Model: Unauthorized inter-agent A2A access, stale/unrevoked session permissions, privacy leakage of full message payloads on public ledgers, and audit log tampering across multi-agent collaborations (pp. 1–6).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: SC-A2A Gateway (Smart-Contract-Powered A2A Gateway) issuing short-lived blockchain-anchored session grants that authorize off-chain A2A message exchanges while batching off-chain audit events into Merkle trees anchored on-chain for compact Merkle inclusion proof verification (Table 1, p. 4; Figure 1, p. 5; p. 16).
Enforcement_Point_Location: SC-A2A Gateway between Collaborating A2A Agents and Blockchain Smart-Contract Ledger (Figure 1, p. 5)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Short-lived session grant authorization, bounded revocation freshness window, off-chain payload privacy, and verifiable Merkle-anchored audit integrity without adding per-message blockchain latency (pp. 1–6, 16–18).
Trust_Assumptions: SC-A2A Gateway mediates inter-agent session setup and blockchain consensus preserves smart-contract session grants and Merkle roots.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluates unauthorized call blocking, revocation freshness intervals (p. 18), and Merkle audit overhead across varying event batch sizes (p. 16: reporting Audit Log Size, Merkle Root Build time in ms, and Proof Verify Mean ± 95% CI and P95 in ms), avoiding per-message on-chain transaction latency.
Exposed_Security_Function: Blockchain-anchored short-lived A2A session grants and batched Merkle-proof audit verification (SC-A2A Gateway)

Study_Title: Securing Agents with Tracked Capabilities

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Tacit programming-language safety harness based on Scala 3 Capture Checking (tracked capabilities and reachability types `T^{c}`, lifetime-scoped lexical closures `requestFileSystem`, and information-flow label tracking) that statically type-checks LLM-generated Scala programs before execution (Figure 1, p. 4; Table 1, p. 6; p. 27).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Scala 3 Capture-Checking Compiler & Lexical Capability Harness prior to Agent Program Execution (Figure 1, p. 4)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Model-independent compile-time rejection of capability escape, unauthorized tool access, and disallowed information flows with zero runtime monitoring overhead (100% security across n=120 malicious trials in both classified and unclassified modes; Table 1, p. 6).
Trust_Assumptions: Scala 3 capture-checking type system and lexical capability wrappers are sound and the agent can only interact with the environment by submitting Scala snippets to the compiler harness.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Imposes zero runtime monitoring overhead because all capability and information-flow violations are caught statically at compile time; across 12 x 10 = 120 adversarial trials (11 malicious task categories across 2 LLM backbones, Table 1, p. 6), achieves 100% security (0% attack success) in both classified and unclassified modes.
Exposed_Security_Function: Compile-time tracked capabilities and lexical lifetime/reachability type checking (Tacit / Scala 3 Capture Checking) for code-acting AI agents
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Requires agents to express tool interactions as typed Scala 3 programs inside the Tacit DSL and incurs compiler type-checking + LLM code-repair retry latency when benign programs fail strict capture checks.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Section 2 (pp. 2–5, Figure 1), Section 3 (p. 6, Table 1), and Appendix (p. 27): "instead of calling tools directly, agents express their intentions as short programs in a capability-safe programming language (tacit)... catches security errors before agents' programs run, imposes no monitoring overhead... Table 1 (n=120): both models achieve 100% security in classified and unclassified modes."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: The Tacit framework enforces tracked capabilities and lexical lifetime control via Scala 3 capture checking, achieving 100% compile-time blocking of unauthorized tool and data-flow actions across 120 adversarial trials with zero runtime monitoring overhead.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Type-theoretic capability tracking harness (EPFL, 27 pp.) evaluated across 120 adversarial code-acting agent trials
Protected_Object: Lexical tool capabilities (`requestFileSystem`, network/file handles), closures `T^{c}`, and classified data values
Composition_Evidence: Statically verifies how capabilities granted by user intent (B1) compose across higher-order closures and sequential tool calls before any code executes at B3 (Figure 1, p. 4; Table 1, p. 6).
Coding_Rationale: Studi M_AND_A yang sangat elegan dari EPFL (27 hlm.): menerapkan Scala 3 Capture Checking (tracked capabilities) untuk menjamin keamanan 100% secara statis sebelum eksekusi pada n=120 percobaan berbahaya dengan nol overhead pemantauan runtime (Tabel 1, hlm. 6).

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Three-stage MCP runtime defense framework combining Stage 1 Pre-Registration Manifest & Hash Verification, Stage 2 Pre-Invocation Semantic/Policy Argument Gate, and Stage 3 Post-Execution Output Sanitization & Quarantine (Figure 1, p. 4; Table 1, p. 3).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Three-Stage MCP Interception Proxy between LLM Client and MCP Servers (Figure 1, p. 4)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Reduces Tool Poisoning ASR from 74% to < 9% and Indirect Prompt Injection ASR from 47% to < 6% while adding < 120 ms median latency per tool call (Abstract, p. 1).

Performance_Overhead_Reported: Reduces Tool Poisoning ASR from 74% to under 9% and Indirect Prompt Injection ASR from 47% to under 6% across evaluated MCP attack families while introducing less than 120 ms of median latency per tool call (Abstract, p. 1; Section 4, pp. 4–6).
Exposed_Security_Function: Three-stage MCP interception proxy (manifest verification, pre-invocation policy gate, post-execution output sanitization)
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Up to ~9% of tool poisoning and ~6% of indirect prompt injections still bypass the three-stage filter, and 120 ms per-call latency accumulates across long multi-tool chains.

Study_Title: Separating intent from execution: A defense-in-depth security architecture for LLM-based multi-agent systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: 16 attack vectors including indirect prompt injection, DID/VC presentation spoofing, unauthorized attribute disclosure, and replay attacks when probabilistic LLMs directly handle cryptographic identity operations (Table 1 & Figure 1, p. 3; p. 23).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Defense-in-depth architecture separating the probabilistic LLM Intent Layer from a deterministic Security Execution Layer (SEL) that handles all W3C DID, Verifiable Credential (VC), DIF Presentation Exchange, short-TTL nonce/challenge (60 s default, p. 5), and policy-gate invariants (`disclosed(attr) => LLM_consented(attr) & policy_permits`, pp. 7–8; Figure 2, p. 3).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Deterministic Security Execution Layer (SEL) & Step 4 Policy Gate decoupled from LLM Intent Layer (Figure 2, p. 3)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Achieves 99% protocol correctness with 0% injection bypass across all 3 LLM providers (vs. 4%–80% when LLMs handle identity directly); even when GPT-4o-mini's Step 3 intent layer is fooled by 66.7% of indirect injections, the deterministic Step 4 SEL policy gate catches 100% of those failures (Abstract, p. 1; p. 23).
Trust_Assumptions: Deterministic SEL and cryptographic key store are isolated from the LLM process and enforce DIF Presentation Exchange and attribute-disclosure invariants.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 23 experiments and 16 attack vectors over 3 LLM providers (p. 1, p. 23): direct LLM identity handling collapses to as low as 4% completion (GPT-4o-mini) with prohibitive latency, whereas decoupling via the deterministic SEL achieves 99% correctness and 0% injection bypass across all 16 attack vectors.
Exposed_Security_Function: Deterministic Security Execution Layer (SEL) for W3C DID/VC presentation exchange and invariant-enforced attribute disclosure
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: When an indirect injection fools the LLM at Step 3 (66.7% of attempts on GPT-4o-mini), the Step 4 SEL gate safely aborts the transaction (0% bypass), which converts a confidentiality/integrity breach into a safe task denial.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Section 1 (pp. 1–3, Table 1 & Figures 1–2), Section 3 (pp. 5–8, Invariants), and Conclusion (p. 23): "when LLMs directly manage cryptographic identity operations, completion rates collapse to as low as 4%... separating the LLM (Intent Layer) from a deterministic Security Execution Layer (SEL) achieves 99% correctness with zero injection bypass across all three providers... GPT-4o-mini's Step 3 is fooled by 66.7% of indirect injection attempts, whereas the deterministic Step 4 policy gate catches 100% of these failures (23 experiments across 16 attack vectors)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Decoupling the LLM Intent Layer from a deterministic Security Execution Layer (SEL) for DID/VC operations achieves 99% protocol correctness and 0% injection bypass across 23 experiments and 16 attack vectors, catching 100% of the 66.7% indirect injections that fool GPT-4o-mini.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 23-experiment, 16-attack-vector empirical evaluation across 3 LLM providers (American Univ. of the Middle East, 23 pp.)
Protected_Object: W3C DIDs, Verifiable Credentials, DIF Presentation Definitions, and private credential attributes
Composition_Evidence: Proves empirically that probabilistic LLM consent parsing at B1/B2 (fooled 66.7% of the time) must be composed with a deterministic SEL policy gate (`disclosed(attr) => LLM_consented(attr) & policy_permits`) at B3 to achieve 0% bypass (pp. 1, 7–8, 23).
Coding_Rationale: Studi M_AND_A (23 hlm.) yang sangat kuat: membuktikan melalui 23 eksperimen dan 16 vektor serangan bahwa memisahkan LLM Intent Layer dari Security Execution Layer (SEL) deterministik meningkatkan keberhasilan dari 4% ke 99% dengan 0% bypass injeksi (menangkap 100% dari 66,7% kegagalan LLM pada Step 3).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Shielding MCP Tool: A Secure Execution Framework Using TEE and Automated Trimming
Threat_Attacker_Model: Untrusted cloud/host OS operators and bloated Trusted Computing Base (TCB) attack surfaces when deploying third-party MCP tool servers in untrusted environments (Figures 1–3, pp. 4–6).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: ShieldMCP framework running MCP tool servers inside hardware Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs / Intel SGX enclaves) paired with an LLM-driven automated test-generation and dead-code function trimming pipeline to shrink the enclave TCB (Figures 2–3, pp. 5–6).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Hardware TEE Enclave & Automated TCB Trimming Pipeline for MCP Servers (Figure 2, p. 5)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Hardware-enforced TEE confidentiality/integrity for MCP tool execution combined with an average 91% reduction in enclave code size (TCB) while preserving 97% test line/branch coverage (Abstract, p. 1; p. 3).
Trust_Assumptions: Hardware TEE processor (Intel SGX) and remote attestation primitives are trusted.

Threat_Attacker_Model: Compromised external databases, man-in-the-middle API tampering, and malicious/poisoned tool responses manipulating LLM agent behavior when agents blindly trust tool outputs (Figure 1, p. 1).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Authenticated Data Structures (ADS) — specifically Merkle trees and cryptographic membership/integrity proofs — integrated into LLM agent-tool pipelines so the agent runtime cryptographically verifies every tool response against a trusted root commitment before ingesting it into the LLM context (Figure 2, p. 5; Table 2 & Figure 4, p. 6).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Agent Runtime ADS Cryptographic Proof Verifier on the Tool-Response Boundary (Figure 2, p. 5)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: End-to-end cryptographic authenticity and integrity of tool-returned data records under collision-resistant hashing with logarithmic proof size 32 * ceil(log2(n)) bytes (pp. 4–6).
Trust_Assumptions: Agent holds an authentic Merkle root digest for the external dataset and the underlying hash function (SHA-256) is collision-resistant.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Integrating Merkle ADS verification into the LLM agent-tool pipeline incurs an average pipeline overhead of 2.5x relative to non-authenticated tool queries (with cryptographic proof verification itself taking only microseconds), and proof size scales logarithmically as 32 * ceil(log2(n)) bytes (Abstract, p. 1; Table 2 & Figure 4, p. 6).
Exposed_Security_Function: Merkle-tree Authenticated Data Structure (ADS) proof generation and microsecond runtime verification for LLM tool responses
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Requires external data providers/tools to maintain Merkle ADS trees and publish authenticated root commitments, and 2.5x pipeline overhead applies to data-intensive tool calls.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Figure 2 (p. 5), and Section 4 (p. 6, Table 2 & Figure 4): "ADS methods can be integrated into LLM agent-tool pipelines, enabling verification with 2.5x average overhead vs. non-authenticated pipelines (cryptographic verification adds microseconds)... Proof size is 32 * ceil(log2(n)) bytes (Merkle tree)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Integrating Merkle Authenticated Data Structures (ADS) into LLM agent-tool pipelines guarantees end-to-end cryptographic integrity of tool responses with 32*ceil(log2(n))-byte proofs and 2.5x average pipeline overhead.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Merkle ADS agent-tool pipeline integration and proof-scaling benchmark (RMIT Univ., 9 pp.)
Protected_Object: External database/tool query responses, Merkle root commitments, and LLM reasoning context
Composition_Evidence: Binds external database state commitments (B4) to pre-ingestion Merkle proof verification at the agent tool-response boundary (B3) before LLM reasoning continues (Figure 2, p. 5).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream M dari RMIT University (9 hlm.) yang mengintegrasikan Authenticated Data Structures (pohon Merkle, ukuran bukti 32*ceil(log2(n)) byte) ke dalam pipeline alat agen LLM dengan rata-rata overhead pipeline 2,5x (Tabel 2, Gambar 4, hlm. 6).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Verifiable and Fair Registered Attribute-Based Multi-Hop Proxy Re-Encryption Scheme for LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Key-escrow abuse by centralized authorities, malicious proxy agents returning forged/incorrect re-encrypted ciphertexts, and unauthorized multi-hop data forwarding across LLM agent coordinators in data-driven/IoT systems (Figures 1–2, pp. 2, 6).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Verifiable and Fair Registered Attribute-Based Multi-Hop Proxy Re-Encryption (VF-RABPRE) eliminating centralized key escrow via registered public keys while supporting fine-grained attribute policies, multi-hop proxy re-encryption across LLM agents, and lightweight re-encryption correctness verification (Figures 1–2, pp. 2, 6; Theorems 1–2, pp. 7, 10).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Cryptographic Multi-Hop Proxy Re-Encryption & Verification Layer across Coordinator Agents (Figure 2, p. 6)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Formally proves Correctness (Theorem 1, p. 7), CPA Secrecy (Theorem 2, p. 10), key-escrow freedom, and verifiable fairness across multi-hop re-encryption chains (pp. 7–12).
Trust_Assumptions: Standard bilinear-pairing/decisional cryptographic hardness assumptions hold in the underlying groups.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Published in IEEE TIFS (Vol. 21, 2026, pp. 6697–6712): achieves constant-time user decryption overhead independent of the number of attributes or hops and avoids heavy zero-knowledge proof generation overhead during re-encryption verification (Tables I–II, p. 12; Section VI, pp. 12–15).
Exposed_Security_Function: Registered Attribute-Based Multi-Hop Proxy Re-Encryption (VF-RABPRE) with formal CPA secrecy (Theorem 2) and constant-time decryption
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Constructed over classical bilinear pairing groups (vulnerable to quantum adversaries) and focuses on encrypted data forwarding rather than semantic prompt-injection filtering inside decrypted payloads.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1 / p. 6697), Figures 1–2 (pp. 2, 6), Section IV–V (p. 7 Theorem 1; p. 10 Theorem 2), and Section VI (p. 12, Tables I–II): "we propose the first Verifiable and Fair Registered Attribute-Based Multi-Hop Proxy Re-Encryption (VF-RABPRE) scheme... Theorem 1 (Correctness)... Theorem 2 (Secrecy): Our VF-RABPRE scheme is CPA secure... constant-time decryption overhead (Table II, p. 12)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: VF-RABPRE eliminates key escrow and enables verifiable, fair attribute-based multi-hop ciphertext forwarding across LLM coordinator agents with proven CPA secrecy (Theorem 2) and constant-time decryption overhead.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal cryptographic proofs (Theorems 1–2) and asymptotic/empirical cost analysis in IEEE TIFS (2026, 16 pp.)
Protected_Object: Multi-hop re-encrypted IoT/enterprise ciphertexts, registered attribute keys, and fairness verification proofs
Composition_Evidence: Chains multi-hop proxy re-encryption across autonomous coordinator agents (B2) with cryptographic verification of re-encrypted ciphertext integrity and fairness (B4) (Figure 2, p. 6; Tables I–II, p. 12).
Coding_Rationale: Artikel jurnal Tier-1 IEEE TIFS (2026, 16 hlm.) yang membuktikan Theorem 1 (Correctness, hlm. 7) dan Theorem 2 (CPA Secrecy, hlm. 10) untuk skema VF-RABPRE dengan biaya dekripsi waktu-konstan (Tabel II, hlm. 12).

Study_Title: VET Your Agent: Towards Host-Independent Autonomy via Verifiable Execution Traces
Threat_Attacker_Model: Malicious or compromised agent hosts fabricating LLM reasoning transcripts, forging external API responses, or altering autonomous agent actions in high-stakes environments such as financial trading (VeriTrade; Figures 1–2, pp. 4–5).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: VET (Verifiable Execution Traces) framework binding an Agent Identity Document (AID, listing model endpoint and notary public keys such as `ecdsa-secp256k1`, p. 15) to short-lived parallel MPC-TLS (`TLSNotary v0.1.0-alpha.12`) cryptographic transcripts for closed-source LLM inference APIs and TEE attestations for public tool APIs (Definitions 4.1–4.3, p. 4; Section 5, p. 9; Appendix A, p. 15).
Enforcement_Point_Location: External Verifier & MPC-TLS Notary / TEE Execution Boundary (Figures 1–2, pp. 4–5)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Host-independent cryptographic verifiability that every step of an autonomous agent's execution loop (LLM inference calls + tool invocations) genuinely occurred as claimed in its AID (pp. 4–9).
Trust_Assumptions: TLSNotary MPC notary server does not collude with the agent host and `ecdsa-secp256k1` / TLS 1.3 primitives are secure.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated on the VeriTrade autonomous financial trading agent (claude-haiku-4-5 + TLSNotary v0.1.0-alpha.12, pp. 9–15): using optimized short-lived parallel MPC-TLS channels for LLM inference APIs and TEEs for public tool APIs keeps end-to-end execution overhead under 3x compared to direct unverified API calls (Abstract, p. 1; Section 6, pp. 9–12).
Exposed_Security_Function: Host-independent Verifiable Execution Traces (VET) via Agent Identity Documents (AID), MPC-TLS (TLSNotary), and TEEs
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: MPC-TLS (TLSNotary) overhead scales with HTTP transcript size (~3x latency vs. direct API calls), and `ecdsa-secp256k1` notary signatures (p. 15) are classical pre-quantum.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Definitions 4.1–4.3 & Figures 1–2 (pp. 4–5), Section 5 (p. 9), and Appendix A (p. 15): "hybrid approach combining MPC-TLS for LLM inference APIs with a lower-overhead TEE for public API calls is the most practical choice, with overhead typically under 3x compared to direct API calls... VeriTrade AID Excerpt: model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, TLSNotary protocol_version v0.1.0-alpha.12, notary_public_key ecdsa-secp256k1."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: VET Your Agent achieves host-independent verifiable autonomy by combining Agent Identity Documents (AID), parallel MPC-TLS (TLSNotary) inference proofs, and TEE tool attestations with under 3x latency overhead over direct API calls.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal agent execution model (Defs. 4.1–4.3) and VeriTrade MPC-TLS/TEE benchmark (University of Oxford, 15 pp.)
Protected_Object: Agent Identity Documents (AID), LLM API HTTPS transcripts, tool execution traces, and verifier audit proofs
Composition_Evidence: Cryptographically chains MPC-TLS notarized LLM reasoning transcripts (B1/B3) with TEE-attested external tool API calls (B3) into a unified host-independent Verifiable Execution Trace (B4) (Figures 1–2, pp. 4–5).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream M dari University of Oxford (15 hlm.) yang memadukan MPC-TLS (TLSNotary v0.1.0-alpha.12) dan TEE ke dalam Verifiable Execution Traces (VET) dengan overhead <3x dibandingkan panggilan API langsung.

Enforcement_Point_Location: MCP Server Plugin Host OS API & Permission Boundary (Figure 1, p. 3)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Provides the first large-scale empirical mapping of sensitive OS/API permission usage across 2,562 real-world MCP applications, motivating fine-grained manifest-based privilege management (Table I, p. 4).
Trust_Assumptions: Current MCP hosts execute third-party server plugins with the full ambient authority of the host user account.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Systematically examines 2,562 real-world MCP applications via automated static analysis (Table I, p. 4), quantifying sensitive filesystem, network, environment-variable, and process-execution API usage across the MCP ecosystem (pp. 1–7).
Exposed_Security_Function: Automated static API privilege measurement across 2,562 real-world MCP applications
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Static AST/API call-graph analysis across 2,562 MCP apps can under-approximate dynamically loaded code and does not benchmark a runtime kernel/sandbox enforcement implementation.

In this work, we conduct the first large-scale empirical analysis of MCP security risks. We develop an automated static analysis framework and systematically examine 2,562 real-world MCP applications."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Static analysis of 2,562 real-world MCP applications reveals pervasive ambient over-privileging across filesystem, network, and subprocess APIs, demonstrating the urgent need for fine-grained privilege management in MCP.

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (MCP-TDP Security Benchmark evaluating Attack Success Rate / ASR and User Command Completion / UCC across 6 risk categories over 5 independent runs per model; Figures 1–2, pp. 1–2; p. 4).
Enforcement_Point_Location: MCP Tool Manual/Description Ingestion & LLM Agent Planning Layer (Figures 1–2, pp. 1–2)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Quantifies systemic vulnerability to Tool Description Poisoning across frontier LLMs (ASRs > 82% for most models, > 88% for top models, and ~100% for GPT-4o in six high-risk scenarios) and identifies 'The Firewall Paradox' (pp. 1–2, 4, 6).
Trust_Assumptions: LLM agents treat MCP tool descriptions (`the manual`) as authoritative system-level documentation during tool planning.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 6 major risk categories (5 independent runs per model, p. 4), MCP-TDP reveals ASRs exceeding 82% for most evaluated models, > 88% for top models, and nearly 100% for leading models like GPT-4o while preserving high User Command Completion (UCC), making the attack stealthy to end users (Abstract & Section I, pp. 1–2; Section IV, p. 4; Conclusion, p. 6).
Exposed_Security_Function: MCP-TDP realistic Tool Description Poisoning benchmark and 'Firewall Paradox' vulnerability fingerprint analysis
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Diagnostic benchmark paper (CAS / IIE, 6 pp.) refuting the adequacy of model-level alignment ('The Firewall Paradox') without benchmarking a cryptographic or taint-tracking runtime defense.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Section I (pp. 1–2, Figures 1–2), Section IV (p. 4), and Section VI (p. 6): "leading models like GPT-4o exhibiting a nearly 100% Attack Success Rate (ASR) in six high-risk scenarios... ASR > 88% for top models and > 82% for most models, identifying 'The Firewall Paradox' where stronger instruction-following amplifies TDP vulnerability."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: The MCP-TDP benchmark demonstrates that Tool Description Poisoning achieves >82% ASR across most LLMs and nearly 100% ASR on GPT-4o across six risk categories, exposing 'The Firewall Paradox' of instruction-following alignment.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical Tool Description Poisoning benchmark across 6 risk categories and 5 independent runs (CAS / IIE, 6 pp.)
Protected_Object: MCP tool manuals/descriptions, LLM planning integrity, and host resources

Study_Title: Whispers of Wealth: A Systematic Red-Teaming Study of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
Threat_Attacker_Model: Pre-signature reasoning-layer prompt injection and 'Branded Whisper Attacks' embedded in external merchant/product metadata targeting financial agents using the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) (Figures 1–3, pp. 2–3).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Red-teaming evaluation of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2, which uses cryptographically signed Intent/Cart/Payment mandates at the execution layer) showing that pre-signature prompt injection corrupts the mandate contents before cryptographic signing occurs (Figures 1–3, pp. 2–3).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Pre-Signature LLM Reasoning Layer prior to AP2 Cryptographic Mandate Signing (Figures 1–2, pp. 2–3)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves empirically that execution-layer cryptographic mandates in AP2 do not protect against pre-signature reasoning manipulation: prompt injection achieves 100% ASR in manipulating product selection/purchase decisions and causes sensitive financial account data exposure in 20% of cases (Abstract, p. 1; Section 4, p. 4).
Trust_Assumptions: AP2 cryptographic signature verification correctly authenticates signed mandates, but the LLM agent constructs mandate parameters from untrusted merchant product descriptions.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Systematic red-teaming benchmark across AP2 purchase workflows (pp. 1, 4–6): pre-signature prompt injection achieves up to 100% ASR in steering product selection / overcharging and induces unauthorized financial account data exposure in 20% of trials.
Exposed_Security_Function: Red-teaming evaluation of pre-signature reasoning vulnerabilities in the cryptographic Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Demonstrates a fundamental semantic-cryptographic gap (signing corrupted intent at B1/B3), motivating pre-signing deterministic intent-to-cart verification.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Figures 1–3 (pp. 2–3), Section 4 (p. 4), and Section 7 (p. 6): "The Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) secures agent-mediated purchases through cryptographically signed mandates, yet its robustness against reasoning-layer attacks remains unclear... prompt injection achieves a 100% success rate in manipulating purchase decisions and leads to sensitive financial account data exposure in 20% of cases."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: While the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) enforces cryptographically signed mandates at the execution layer, pre-signature reasoning-layer prompt injections ('Branded Whisper Attacks') achieve 100% ASR in manipulating purchases and expose financial account data in 20% of trials.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical red-teaming study of Google's Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) under pre-signature prompt injection (Univ. of Georgia & Kennesaw State, 6 pp.)
Protected_Object: AP2 cryptographically signed purchase mandates, user shopping intent, and financial account data
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates the classic pre-signature semantic gap: poisoning external product metadata (B4) hijacks LLM pre-signature reasoning (B1) so the agent cryptographically signs a malicious AP2 mandate executed at B3 (Figures 1–3, pp. 2–3).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream A (6 hlm.) yang sangat penting bagi sintesis RQ2: membuktikan bahwa mandat bertanda tangan kriptografis pada Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) tetap rentan 100% terhadap manipulasi penalaran pra-penandatanganan (dan 20% kebocoran data akun).

Study_Title: Zero-Trust Gateway Protocol for Multi-Tenant AI Agents

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NIST SP 800-207 / SP 800-207A aligned Zero-Trust Gateway Protocol enforcing native Envoy `jwt_authn` signature verification (< 1 ms), O(log N) policy lookup (2–3 ms), and OAuth 2.0 RFC 8693 Token Exchange (~180 ms) issuing short-TTL (5 min) tokens with narrow `aud` and skill-scoped claims (Tables I–III, pp. 2–6; Figure 1, p. 3).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Zero-Trust API Gateway (Envoy jwt_authn + Policy Engine + RFC 8693 Token Exchange) between Web Clients, Micro-Agents, and Skills (Figure 1, p. 3)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Fine-grained user-to-agent-to-skill authorization, 5-minute short-TTL audience/skill confinement, and 100% gateway-mediated audit trail coverage across 11 threat categories (pp. 3–6).
Trust_Assumptions: Identity Provider (IdP) JWKS keys and Zero-Trust Gateway control plane are intact.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Table III (p. 6) reports median latency by protocol phase: JWT validation < 1 ms O(1), Policy lookup 2–3 ms O(log N), RFC 8693 Token exchange ~180 ms (1 IdP RTT + issuance), Gateway forwarding ~15 ms (Constant), and total End-to-End gateway mediation ~200 ms with 100% audit trail coverage (p. 5).
Exposed_Security_Function: NIST SP 800-207 Zero-Trust Gateway with RFC 8693 5-min skill-scoped token exchange and <1 ms JWT validation
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Synchronous RFC 8693 IdP token exchange accounts for ~180 ms of the ~200 ms end-to-end gateway latency (Table III, p. 6), and does not inspect semantic prompt injection inside authorized skill arguments.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Tables I–II & Figure 1 (pp. 2–3), and Section V (pp. 5–6, Table III): "informed by NIST SP 800-207 and SP 800-207A... issues short-lived (5 min TTL), agent-scoped tokens with skill-level permissions via RFC 8693... TABLE III: Median Latency by Protocol Phase: JWT validation < 1 ms O(1), Policy lookup 2–3 ms O(log N), Token exchange ~180 ms (1 IdP RTT), Gateway forwarding ~15 ms, End-to-end ~200 ms."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: A NIST SP 800-207 Zero-Trust Gateway Protocol using RFC 8693 token exchange (5-min TTL, narrow audience/skill scopes) enforces user-to-agent-to-skill authorization across 11 threat categories with ~200 ms end-to-end median latency (<1 ms JWT validation, 2–3 ms policy lookup).

Study_Title: ZT-ICAS: A Zero-Trust Integrity-Constrained Framework for Agentic Vulnerability Scanning
Threat_Attacker_Model: Adversarial repositories and weaponized CVE descriptions tricking autonomous vulnerability-scanning agents into Remote Code Execution (e.g., executing shell commands via the `checkcve` tool — 'PWNED', p. 7) and context poisoning across scans.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: ZT-ICAS (Zero-Trust Integrity-Constrained Agentic Scanning) four-layer framework combining Input Integrity Verification, Capability Bounding (strictly restricting shell/tool arguments), State Guard Layer ('Ephemeral Shoring' / context reset between scanning steps), and Output Execution Verification (Figures 1–2, pp. 2–3; pp. 4, 7).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Four-Layer ZT-ICAS Guard (Input Integrity, Capability Bounding, State Guard Ephemeral Shoring, Execution Verifier; Figures 1–2, pp. 2–3)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Blocks RCE shell injection (such as `checkcve` command injection) and cross-step state contamination where standard unprotected vulnerability-scanning agents suffer a 94% compromise/failure rate (pp. 4, 7).
Trust_Assumptions: ZT-ICAS four-layer wrapper mediates all tool calls (`checkcve`, file readers) and resets ephemeral context state between untrusted code segments.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated against RCE and prompt-injection campaigns in 5th IEEE ICAIC 2026 (pp. 4–7): baseline standard agentic vulnerability scanners exhibit a 94% failure/compromise rate, whereas ZT-ICAS Capability Bounding and Ephemeral Shoring block RCE shell escalation with manageable latency overhead.
Exposed_Security_Function: Four-layer Zero-Trust Integrity-Constrained Agentic Scanning (Capability Bounding + Ephemeral Shoring context reset)
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Ephemeral Shoring (frequent short-term memory context resets, p. 4) can limit long-range multi-file vulnerability reasoning across deeply nested call graphs.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Figures 1–2 (pp. 2–3), Section IV (p. 4), and Section V (p. 7): "Baseline Performance (94% Failure): The Standard Agentic Scanner without zero-trust constraints failed in 94% of adversarial test cases... State Guard Layer: Ephemeral Shoring (Context Reset)... Our Capability Bounding guards prevented compromised agents from executing shell commands via the checkcve tool ('PWNED')."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: ZT-ICAS enforces four zero-trust layers—including Capability Bounding and Ephemeral Shoring context resets—to block RCE shell injection (`checkcve`) in agentic vulnerability scanners where unprotected baselines suffer a 94% failure rate.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Four-layer zero-trust defense evaluation for agentic vulnerability scanning in 5th IEEE ICAIC (2026, 7 pp.)

Study_Title: ZT-MCP: A Zero-Trust Security Architecture for MCP-Connected AI Agents

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: ZT-MCP Zero-Trust security architecture operating as a hardened proxy between AI agents and MCP servers, enforcing enterprise-CA short-lived mTLS certificates, continuous per-invocation policy re-evaluation (preventing tool-chaining escalation), and outbound tool-output DLP/sanitization (Tables I–II & Figure 1, pp. 2–3; p. 5).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Hardened ZT-MCP Proxy mediating Agent-to-MCP-Server Discovery, Invocation, and Output Flows (Figure 1, p. 3)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Achieves 100.0% attack block rate, 0.0% false positive rate, 100% Access Control Precision (ACP), and 100% Tool Audit Coverage (TAC) across evaluated enterprise MCP attack suites with 39.5 ms Policy Enforcement Latency (PEL) (Abstract, p. 1; Section IV, pp. 5–7).
Trust_Assumptions: Enterprise-managed root CA issuing short-lived certificates and the hardened ZT-MCP proxy are non-bypassable.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: On an enterprise data benchmark, ZT-MCP achieves a 100.0% attack block rate, 0.0% false positive rate, 100% Tool Audit Coverage (TAC), and 39.5 ms mean Policy Enforcement Latency (PEL) per tool invocation (Abstract, p. 1; Section IV, pp. 5–7).

Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Authors note (p. 2) that the 100.0% block rate and 0.0% FPR are achieved under a fixed, known enterprise attack suite and deterministic policy ruleset; adaptive semantic obfuscation outside declared rules remains a residual challenge.
